---
title: Modify cache key
description: Choose request variables that separate cached objects on a CDN resource and manage cache key modification settings.
---

import { MethodSwitch, MethodSection } from "/snippets/method-switch.jsx";

<MethodSwitch>
  <MethodSection id="portal" label="Customer Portal">

<p>Select which request variables separate cached objects on a CDN resource. Requests that produce the same key share one cached object.</p>

## Cache key modification

<p>Save the selection as **Cache key modification** on the CDN resource.</p>

<Warning>
Enabling or changing cache key modification can invalidate cached objects and reduce the cache hit ratio. [Purge&nbsp;by&nbsp;pattern](/cdn/clear-cdn-resource-cache-by-url-pattern-or-all) is unavailable while this option is enabled.
</Warning>

<Steps>
  <Step title="Reach the resource list">
    In the [Gcore Customer Portal](https://portal.gcore.com), navigate to **CDN**. The **CDN resources** page opens.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Select the resource">
    Click the resource CNAME.

    <Frame>![CDN resource CNAME in the resources list](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/modify-cache-key/cdn-resource-name.png)</Frame>
  </Step>
  <Step title="Find cache key modification">
    In the **Cache** section, click **Cache key modification**.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Set the variables">
    Turn on the **Enable cache key modification** toggle and add variables from [Supported&nbsp;variables](#supported-variables).

    <Frame>![Cache key modification settings](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/modify-cache-key/cache-key-modification-section.png)</Frame>
  </Step>
  <Step title="Save the cache key">
    Click **Save changes**.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Supported variables

<p>Include a variable when its values must be cached as separate objects.</p>

- `$request_uri`: Full original request URI, including the query string. With the [rewrite&nbsp;feature](/cdn/cdn-resource-options/rewrite-redirect-requests-from-the-cdn-to-the-origin), this variable keeps the original URI rather than the rewritten path.
- `$scheme`: Request protocol.
- `$uri`: Normalized request URI. The value can change during request processing, including internal redirects and index files.
- `$http_x_cdn_real_host`: Original Host header passed through the CDN. It splits the cache across aliases on one resource.

## Interactions and limitations

<p>These combinations change which requests still share one object.</p>

- If the key includes both `$uri` and `$request_uri`, the query string remains part of the cache key because `$request_uri` includes it.
- When **Redirect HTTP to HTTPS** is enabled, `$scheme` does not create separate HTTP and HTTPS cache variants, because HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS.
- `$uri` overrides [Ignore&nbsp;query&nbsp;string](/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/ignore-the-set-cookie-or-query-string-parameters-when-caching-content-on-cdn-servers).
- Administrator-restricted cache keys stay as set by Gcore. [Contact&nbsp;support](mailto:support@gcore.com) to request a change.

</MethodSection>
  <MethodSection id="api" label="REST API">

<p>Set `proxy_cache_key` to select which request variables separate cached objects. Find the resource ID in [list&nbsp;CDN&nbsp;resources](/api-reference/cdn/cdn-resources/list-cdn-resources).</p>

<Info>
An [API&nbsp;token](/account-settings/api-tokens) is required.
</Info>

<p>Open a terminal and export the required variables:</p>

```bash
export GCORE_API_KEY="{YOUR_API_KEY}"
export CDN_RESOURCE_ID="{YOUR_RESOURCE_ID}"
```

## Cache key

<p>`value` joins the variables that should separate cached objects. Each variable appears at most once, with no separator between them.</p>

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `$request_uri` | Full original request URI, including the query string. With the [rewrite&nbsp;feature](/cdn/cdn-resource-options/rewrite-redirect-requests-from-the-cdn-to-the-origin), this variable keeps the original URI |
| `$scheme` | Request protocol, `http` or `https` |
| `$uri` | Normalized request URI. The value can change during request processing. This variable overrides [Ignore&nbsp;query&nbsp;string](/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/ignore-the-set-cookie-or-query-string-parameters-when-caching-content-on-cdn-servers) |
| `$http_x_cdn_real_host` | Original Host header. It splits the cache across aliases on one resource |

- If the key includes both `$uri` and `$request_uri`, the query string remains part of the cache key because `$request_uri` includes it.
- When **Redirect HTTP to HTTPS** is enabled, `$scheme` does not create separate HTTP and HTTPS cache variants, because HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS.
- Administrator-restricted cache keys stay as set by Gcore. [Contact&nbsp;support](mailto:support@gcore.com) to request a change.

<Warning>
Enabling or changing cache key modification can invalidate cached objects and reduce the cache hit ratio. [Purge&nbsp;by&nbsp;pattern](/cdn/clear-cdn-resource-cache-by-url-pattern-or-all) is unavailable while this option is enabled.
</Warning>

<p>Unsupported variables, a repeated variable, or other text return HTTP 400.</p>

<p>`enabled` and `value` are both required. A blank `value` returns HTTP 400.</p>

<p>Send `proxy_cache_key` with `enabled` true. Variable order matters: `$scheme$uri` and `$uri$scheme` produce different cache key strings.</p>

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Python SDK">
    ```python
    import os
    from gcore import Gcore

    client = Gcore()

    resource = client.cdn.cdn_resources.update(
        int(os.environ["CDN_RESOURCE_ID"]),
        options={
            "proxy_cache_key": {"enabled": True, "value": "$scheme$uri"},
        },
    )
    print(resource.options.proxy_cache_key.enabled, resource.options.proxy_cache_key.value)
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Go SDK">
    ```go
    package main

    import (
        "context"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "strconv"

        gcore "github.com/G-Core/gcore-go"
        "github.com/G-Core/gcore-go/cdn"
    )

    func main() {
        client := gcore.NewClient()
        ctx := context.Background()
        resourceID, err := strconv.ParseInt(os.Getenv("CDN_RESOURCE_ID"), 10, 64)
        if err != nil {
            panic(err)
        }

        resource, err := client.CDN.CDNResources.Update(ctx, resourceID, cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParams{
            Options: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptions{
                ProxyCacheKey: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptionsProxyCacheKey{
                    Enabled: true,
                    Value:   "$scheme$uri",
                },
            },
        })
        if err != nil {
            panic(err)
        }
        fmt.Println(resource.Options.ProxyCacheKey.Enabled, resource.Options.ProxyCacheKey.Value)
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="curl">
    ```bash
    curl -X PATCH "https://api.gcore.com/cdn/resources/$CDN_RESOURCE_ID" \
      -H "Authorization: APIKey $GCORE_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "options": {
          "proxy_cache_key": {
            "enabled": true,
            "value": "$scheme$uri"
          }
        }
      }'
    ```

    <p>The API returns HTTP 200:</p>

    ```json
    {
      "id": 12345,
      "options": {
        "proxy_cache_key": {
          "enabled": true,
          "value": "$scheme$uri"
        }
      }
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<p>Set `enabled` to false to turn cache key modification off. `value` remains required, and the stored string stays in place.</p>

<Note>
In the Go SDK, set `Value` to an allowed non-empty string when `Enabled` is false. An empty `Value` is omitted, and the stored option stays unchanged.
</Note>

</MethodSection>
  <MethodSection id="terraform" label="Terraform">

<p>Set `proxy_cache_key` so selected request variables separate cached objects, using the [Terraform&nbsp;provider](/developer-tools/terraform/overview) v2. Requests that produce the same key share one cached object.</p>

<p>`value` joins the allowed variables with no separator, and each variable appears at most once. The allowed variables are `$http_x_cdn_real_host` (original Host header), `$request_uri` (full original request URI, including the query string), `$scheme` (request protocol), and `$uri` (normalized request URI). A blank `value`, a repeated variable, or any other text returns HTTP 400. Leaving `proxy_cache_key` out of `options` leaves the stored option unchanged. Run `terraform apply` after editing `options`.</p>

<p>With the [rewrite&nbsp;feature](/cdn/cdn-resource-options/rewrite-redirect-requests-from-the-cdn-to-the-origin), `$request_uri` keeps the original URI rather than the rewritten path. If the key includes both `$uri` and `$request_uri`, the query string stays in the key because `$request_uri` includes it. When **Redirect HTTP to HTTPS** is enabled, `$scheme` does not create separate HTTP and HTTPS variants, because HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS. `$uri` overrides [Ignore&nbsp;query&nbsp;string](/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/ignore-the-set-cookie-or-query-string-parameters-when-caching-content-on-cdn-servers). Administrator-restricted cache keys stay as set by Gcore. [Contact&nbsp;support](mailto:support@gcore.com) to request a change.</p>

<Warning>
Enabling or changing cache key modification can invalidate cached objects and reduce the cache hit ratio. [Purge&nbsp;by&nbsp;pattern](/cdn/clear-cdn-resource-cache-by-url-pattern-or-all) is unavailable while this option is enabled.
</Warning>

## Cache key

<p>Set `enabled` to true. `$scheme$uri` and `$uri$scheme` are stored as different keys.</p>

```hcl
resource "gcore_cdn_origin_group" "example" {
  name = "my-origin-group"

  sources = [
    {
      source  = "example.com"
      enabled = true
    }
  ]
}

resource "gcore_cdn_resource" "example" {
  cname           = "cdn.example.com"
  origin_group    = gcore_cdn_origin_group.example.id
  origin_protocol = "HTTPS"

  options = {
    proxy_cache_key = {
      enabled = true
      value   = "$scheme$uri"
    }
  }
}
```

### Turn cache key modification off

<p>Set `enabled` to false and keep `value`. Cache key modification is off, and the stored string stays in place. This configuration keeps `$scheme$uri`.</p>

```hcl
resource "gcore_cdn_origin_group" "example" {
  name = "my-origin-group"

  sources = [
    {
      source  = "example.com"
      enabled = true
    }
  ]
}

resource "gcore_cdn_resource" "example" {
  cname           = "cdn.example.com"
  origin_group    = gcore_cdn_origin_group.example.id
  origin_protocol = "HTTPS"

  options = {
    proxy_cache_key = {
      enabled = false
      value   = "$scheme$uri"
    }
  }
}
```

</MethodSection>
</MethodSwitch>
